stages.label: Apply
stages.detail: Requires 3+ years of relevant post-undergrad work experience before the MBA

stages.label: Assessment
stages.detail: Online Assessment that 'puts you in real Amazon situations' (work-style/situational, not a live interview)

stages.label: Phone screen
stages.detail: Not listed on Amazon's MBA page. Amazon's general guidance: 1–2 phone screens are typical. PM prep page (all PM roles): 60 min with a senior leader, half Leadership Principles behavioral, half functional PM.

stages.label: Interview loop
stages.detail: Individual 1:1s with employees, Leadership Principles based, incl. a Bar Raiser. PM prep page (all PM roles): five 55-min interviews plus a writing assessment due ~2 days before; Full-time PM loop also covers product mgmt and stakeholder mgmt competencies

stages.label: Offer
stages.detail: Result within five business days of the interview

amazon.distinctive: Every interview is anchored on the Leadership Principles, and a Bar Raiser from outside the hiring team sits in on the loop.
amazon.caveat: Amazon's MBA page lists the steps; screen and loop detail comes from its full-time PM prep page, so intern loops may be shorter. Amazon's MBA FAQ: you're considered for one role at a time, and without an offer you're no longer eligible for MBA-level roles that cycle.

stages.label: Apply
stages.detail: Up to 3 applications per 30 days. MBA applications open Sept–Oct; interviews rolling

stages.label: Assessment
stages.detail: May be asked to take the Google Hiring Assessment (workstyle)

stages.label: Recruiter chat
stages.detail: Typically 1–2 shorter phone/video conversations with the recruiter that assess key skills

stages.label: Interviews
stages.detail: Panel of interviews over video or in person, scored on rubrics; role-related, open-ended questions, no brainteasers. Some roles assign a small project (e.g. a case study) before interviews.

stages.label: Review
stages.detail: Application and interviews reviewed together. Secondary guides (full-time PM) call this the hiring committee; team matching may come before or after it.

stages.label: Team match
stages.detail: MBA intern posting: candidates matched with teams based on background and skills

stages.label: Offer
stages.detail: Process typically ~6–8 weeks

google.distinctive: MBA interns are placed on a team after interviews, based on background and skills; the decision comes from a review of your whole packet, not any one interviewer.
google.caveat: Google doesn't publish interview counts or lengths.

stages.label: Screening call
stages.detail: All-roles page: 'in some cases' a brief screening conversation before interview invites; for students the first round itself is called the screen.

stages.label: First round
stages.detail: Initial virtual interview (first-round screen); you're assessed for a functional role (e.g. PM) across all teams that hire for it.

stages.label: Final round
stages.detail: Virtual interview day: 1:1s with breaks; behavioral and functional/technical questions; you're assessed for a specific role or org, then team-matched. 1:1 meetings with employees, breaks between; general hiring page says 2–4 conversations of up to an hour; PM intern (non-MBA guide): ~3 × 45–60 min mixing behavioral, product sense and technical fluency

stages.label: Offer
stages.detail: Recruiter shares timeline; offer documents by email

microsoft.distinctive: Two official rounds for students, an initial and a final, and every interview is virtual.
microsoft.caveat: The PM final-round mix comes from a third-party prep guide that doesn't distinguish MBA interns. Microsoft says decisions can take up to 90 days and it can't expedite for competing offer deadlines.

stages.label: Recruiter call
stages.detail: 30–60 min phone screen with a recruiter

stages.label: Hiring manager
stages.detail: Interview with a hiring manager and team member covering work experience and educational focus

stages.label: Panel + presentation
stages.detail: Typically a panel interview or case study where you present a previous project and accomplishments

stages.label: Offer
stages.detail: Salesforce's all-roles FAQ: most interviews are virtual (Google Meet), but an on-site at a Salesforce office is required before an offer. Not mentioned on the MBA-intern page.

salesforce.distinctive: The final round is a panel where you present a past project of your own. Salesforce's general hiring FAQ also requires an on-site visit before any offer.
salesforce.caveat: Salesforce's university-recruiting page appears to date from about 2018, so the MBA steps may be out of date. The on-site requirement comes from Salesforce's all-roles hiring FAQ.

stages.label: Recruiter call
stages.detail: Not described on the official page. Aced (PM guide, not intern-specific) lists recruiter calls, then phone interviews, then a 2-hour take-home before the final round.

stages.label: Craft demo
stages.detail: 60 min with 4 hiring-team members: short personal intro, then present a case study built for the role

stages.label: Assessors
stages.detail: 45 min with 2 assessors: skills, experience and follow-ups on your case study

stages.label: Team member
stages.detail: 30 min with a cross-functional colleague, focused on Intuit values

stages.label: Manager
stages.detail: 30–60 min with a people manager: motivation, successes and learnings

stages.label: Decision
stages.detail: Intuit commits to feedback within 24 hours of the interview

intuit.distinctive: The final round opens with a 'craft demo', where you present a case study to the hiring team before the 1:1 interviews.
intuit.caveat: Intuit describes only the final round; the recruiter call is from a prep guide.

stages.label: Recruiter call
stages.detail: Recruiter phone screen on experience and the role

stages.label: Work exercise
stages.detail: Role-specific (your recruiter tells you if it's required): a task mirroring the role, e.g. an analytics task, written exercise or work simulation. In some roles it comes before the recruiter screen.

stages.label: Team interview
stages.detail: 'Business interview' with hiring managers or team members; be ready to solve problems live. Internship FAQ: interviews typically last 30–60 min, with 2–4 stages depending on the role.

uber.distinctive: Uber's full-time Product guide describes a 'Jam Session' (a take-home assignment you present) run alongside a 3–4 interview loop. Uber doesn't say whether MBA PM interns get it.
uber.caveat: Uber's internship guide is generic (written mostly for university students) and doesn't describe an MBA-specific process. The Jam Session is from Uber's full-time Product guide.

stages.label: Apply
stages.detail: Create an Adobe candidate profile and apply

stages.label: Talent call
stages.detail: Conversation with a Talent team member on background and career goals

stages.label: Hiring manager
stages.detail: Hiring manager probes background, problem-solving and fit with the role

stages.label: Skills + team
stages.detail: Further interviews with team members and partners, plus role-dependent skills assessments (e.g. technical, sales scenario, design thinking)

adobe.caveat: Adobe's hiring page covers all roles and says nothing MBA-specific.

cisco.roleScope: All Cisco roles (no MBA-specific official guide)

stages.label: Apply
stages.detail: Online application; recruiters first check that minimum qualifications are visible on the resume.

stages.label: Recruiter chat
stages.detail: If selected, a recruiter reaches out to learn about you and explain the process.

stages.label: Interviews
stages.detail: Format varies by team and role. Cisco's early-careers page says non-engineering roles may include behavioral interviews and a writing assessment.

stages.label: Offer
stages.detail: After reviewing interview feedback, the recruiter extends an offer.

cisco.distinctive: Cisco's MBA postings are pipeline ads: a Cisco representative may contact you if a relevant role opens.
cisco.caveat: Cisco's pages aren't MBA-specific, and nothing says whether MBA PM or strategy loops use cases or product questions.

dell.roleScope: All Dell roles (no MBA-specific official guide)

stages.label: Apply
stages.detail: Apply online; screening for most roles is done within about four weeks of posting.

stages.label: Recruiter screen
stages.detail: If selected, a recruiter contacts you to screen.

stages.label: Interviews
stages.detail: Conversations about team fit, Dell's values and your career goals. They can be virtual (InterviewStream) or onsite. Dell asks for specific examples of past behavior that show the competencies the role needs.

stages.label: Decision
stages.detail: Dell's FAQ says interviewed candidates hear the outcome within 14 days (its hiring page says it 'strives' to).

dell.distinctive: Dell publishes service commitments: screening within about 4 weeks of posting and an outcome within 14 days of interviewing.
dell.caveat: These are Dell's general hiring pages, not MBA-specific; no reputable source describes MBA PM or marketing interview content. Dell doesn't contact candidates who aren't selected for a screen or interview.

stages.label: Application
stages.detail: Online application; status tracked in candidate portal

stages.label: Screening
stages.detail: IBMers in the field review skills and experience

stages.label: Online assess.
stages.detail: One or two role-dependent assessments: a recorded video interview, a multiple-choice or coding test, and/or an English test.

stages.label: Interview
stages.detail: Structured/behavioral interviews by phone, video or in person; AI-First posting lets you state a preferred team during interviews Or an assessment-center visit (group exercise plus in-person interview).

stages.label: Decision
stages.detail: Offer and onboarding

ibm.distinctive: IBM's application page describes structured/behavioral interviews, but its entry-level consulting guide says consulting candidates typically get a first-round case interview, then a behavioral round.
ibm.caveat: IBM's official pages cover the generic process and entry-level (not MBA) consulting. Whether MBA strategy interns or FLDP get a case round isn't confirmed, so prepare for one. Postings say IBM won't sponsor visas for these roles.

paypal.roleScope: MBA internships (general PayPal process plus older PM MBA posting)

stages.label: Skills test
stages.detail: A Product Manager Intern – MBA posting (Summer 2023 cycle) said applicants complete a HackerRank skills assessment before a University Recruiter follows up. Not confirmed for current non-PM MBA roles.

stages.label: Recruiter call
stages.detail: A recruiter phones to discuss the role and your experience.

stages.label: Team rounds
stages.detail: Interviews with team members, held virtually on Microsoft Teams. PayPal advises preparing specific, detailed examples.

stages.label: Next steps
stages.detail: After all interviews, the recruiter follows up on next steps.

paypal.distinctive: Older PM MBA postings put a HackerRank skills assessment before any recruiter contact.
paypal.caveat: PayPal's official page covers all hiring, not MBA interns specifically. The HackerRank step comes from a Summer 2023 PM MBA posting. No source describes case interviews or the number of rounds for current MBA roles.

servicenow.roleScope: All roles (company-wide hiring process); MBA PM posting adds application tips

stages.label: Application
stages.detail: Apply on ServiceNow's careers site. For the MBA PM roles, put your Inbound vs Outbound preference and years of experience in the hiring-manager notes.

stages.label: Interviews
stages.detail: Interviews about your skills and values. Depending on the role they may include a technical coding assessment or a presentation. AI help is not allowed unless they say otherwise.

stages.label: Decision
stages.detail: The hiring team debriefs, then you get an offer or feedback.

servicenow.distinctive: In the Summer 2026 cycle, pM interns are hired into Inbound (build and roadmap) or Outbound (go-to-market and evangelism) PM tracks. Candidates state a preference and may be considered for both.
servicenow.caveat: The official page describes ServiceNow's general three-step process, not MBA-intern rounds specifically. No reliable source was found for the number or content of MBA PM interview rounds. ServiceNow's own FAQ points intern candidates to its Early Career page, which gives no interview details.

tiktok.roleScope: Early-career roles generally (incl. MBA interns); not MBA-specific

stages.label: Resume screen
stages.detail: Rolling review in order of application; max two applications per application period (Jan–Jun, Jul–Dec), counting TikTok and affiliates globally.

stages.label: Assessment
stages.detail: Online assessment 'if applicable'; depends on role and region. Can be a virtual or in-person exercise, sometimes with other candidates

stages.label: Team interviews
stages.detail: Several interviews with the hiring team, mostly online. Expect background, why-TikTok and role-specific questions

tiktok.distinctive: Some MBA roles ask for more than the usual: the 2027 Ads PM intern posting requires Chinese and English, for meetings with Mandarin-speaking engineering teams.
tiktok.caveat: One forum anecdote (PracHub, July 2025, not stated to be MBA) describes four rounds for a PM intern: background, behavioral, a tough manager round, and HR; some interviewers switched to Chinese. Unverified.

stages.label: Resume review
stages.detail: Recruiting reviews the application and reaches out if there's a match.

stages.label: Recruiter call
stages.detail: Initial conversation with a sourcer or recruiter; a good time to ask about timeline.

stages.label: Phone screens
stages.detail: 1–2 behavioral and/or technical phone or video interviews with a potential peer or manager: behavioral, hypothetical and case-based questions.

stages.label: Virtual onsite
stages.detail: Up to five ~45-minute interviews with potential teammates and cross-functional partners; content mix not specified.

waymo.distinctive: Waymo explicitly bans AI assistance in live interviews. Its tips stress clarifying questions, framing and breaking down problems, and examples of handling ambiguity and gaining alignment in a matrixed org.
waymo.caveat: The official page describes Waymo's general process, not MBA internships; the early-careers page gives no intern-specific process. Whether Strategic Finance includes a modeling test isn't stated.
